The state distribution shows a relatively balanced split between Closed (259 incidents) and Resolved (241 incidents), indicating that nearly half of the incidents were resolved but not necessarily closed.

When examining the combination of category and priority, Hardware incidents show a stark imbalance with 207 High priority cases compared to just 103 Critical priority cases, while other categories like Database and Software have more balanced distributions between High and Critical priorities.

WITH cost_warranty AS (
    SELECT 
        asset_tag,
        cost,
        DATEDIFF('day', CAST(purchased_on AS DATE), CAST(warranty_expiration AS DATE)) AS warranty_days,
        model_category,
        department
    FROM data
    WHERE warranty_expiration IS NOT NULL AND purchased_on IS NOT NULL
),
avg_warranty_by_cost AS (
    SELECT 
        cost,
        AVG(warranty_days) AS avg_warranty_for_cost
    FROM cost_warranty
    GROUP BY cost
)
SELECT 
    cw.asset_tag,
    cw.cost,
    cw.warranty_days,
    cw.avg_warranty_for_cost,
    (cw.warranty_days - cw.avg_warranty_for_cost) AS diff_from_avg
FROM cost_warranty cw
JOIN avg_warranty_by_cost aw ON cw.cost = aw.cost
WHERE ABS(cw.warranty_days - cw.avg_warranty_for_cost) > 500
ORDER BY ABS(cw.warranty_days - cw.avg_warranty_for_cost) DESC

insights: The IT department has the highest expense rejection rate at 44.2%, more than double the next highest department (HR at 14.3%).
The Miscellaneous category has the highest expense rejection rate at 17.6%, indicating potential issues with how these expenses are categorized or approved.
The rejection rate spiked significantly in February 2024 at 19.0%, which is more than triple the average monthly rejection rate of about 6%.
Vernon Engelman has the highest individual rejection rate at 53.8%, which is more than 10 times higher than the next highest user (Helene Iberg at 41.2%).

Within the IT department, Assets category has the highest rejection rate at 56.5%, which is significantly higher than other categories, suggesting specific issues with asset-related expense approvals.
The largest individual expense amounts that were rejected are $936, $3456, $8084, $4544, and $7663, all occurring only once, suggesting these might be outliers rather than systemic issues.

There is a notable discrepancy in procurement strategy between departments, with HR having the highest average asset cost ($4,358) but only moderate warranty periods (987 days), while Customer Support has lower average costs ($3,106) but the shortest warranty periods (920 days).

Assets are distributed across four cost buckets with clear patterns: low-cost items (<$1000) have the shortest average warranty period (about 300 days), while very high-cost items (> $6000) have the longest warranty periods (about 1,095 days), indicating a strong correlation between price and warranty length.

4. Temporal Warranty Trends: Warranty periods have steadily increased over time, from 383 days in May 2023 to 1,159 days in April 2024.

5. Top Asset Assignees: Nadia Wilshire has the highest number of assets assigned (7) with an average warranty of 653 days.

6. Expensive Asset Analysis: Dell PowerEdge R730 Servers are the most expensive ($11,943) with a 561-day warranty period.

7. Expired Warranty Patterns: Among expired warranties, Server models have the highest average cost ($8,493) but shortest warranty period (511 days).

These insights suggest that procurement decisions should consider both cost and warranty duration, with particular attention to the trend toward longer warranties over time and the significant variation in warranty periods across different asset types and departments.
